prompt:
Implement `ArchitectureClient.java` as a single-file Java client that produces the deployable architecture artifacts for the VMware Cloud Foundation project below. The protected `TestMain` harness calls `ArchitectureClient.generate(Path inventory, Path compatibilitySnapshot, Path outputDirectory)`, so preserve that exact public static method signature and use only the Java standard library.

This is a VCF 9.1 greenfield management-domain design at CHI1 plus an ordered migration plan for the existing OMA1 estate in `fixtures/estate-inventory.json`. Each available host has 32 licensed physical cores, 512 GiB RAM, and 10 TiB raw NVMe. CHI1 has six new hosts named `chi1-esx01` through `chi1-esx06`; OMA1 can supply four equivalent hosts. The management workload requires 120 cores, 2,048 GiB RAM, and 24 TiB usable storage after any one host fails. Use vSAN ESA with failures-to-tolerate 1. CHI1 and OMA1 have 4 ms round-trip latency. The recovery requirement is RPO 15 minutes and RTO 4 hours.

The customer's VCF subscription entitles exactly 192 physical cores across the management-domain topology. All cores of every participating host count. The pinned compatibility snapshot says that both a single-site management domain and a 4+4 host stretched management domain are technically supported at 4 ms, so licensing removes the otherwise valid stretched topology. Produce a six-host single-site CHI1 management domain and use OMA1 as an asynchronous backup-and-restore recovery site. Do not silently model OMA1 hosts as members of the greenfield management cluster.

Use these deployment values: SDDC id `chi1-m01`, VCF instance `central-vcf`, workflow `VCF`, version `9.1.0.0`, DNS suffix `corp.example`, DNS servers `10.20.0.10` and `10.20.0.11`, and NTP servers `10.20.0.20` and `10.20.0.21`. Configure VLAN-backed networks MANAGEMENT/110 (`10.20.10.0/24`, gateway `10.20.10.1`, host range `.31`-`.36`), VMOTION/120 (`10.20.20.0/24`, gateway `10.20.20.1`, range `.31`-`.36`), VSAN/130 (`10.20.30.0/24`, gateway `10.20.30.1`, range `.31`-`.36`), VM_MANAGEMENT/140 (`10.20.40.0/24`, gateway `10.20.40.1`, range `.20`-`.39`), and FLEET_MANAGEMENT/150 (`10.20.50.0/24`, gateway `10.20.50.1`, range `.20`-`.31`, exactly 12 addresses). Use a single 9000-MTU DVS with `vmnic0`/`uplink1` and `vmnic1`/`uplink2`. Deploy vCenter `chi1-vc01.corp.example`, SDDC Manager `chi1-sddc01.corp.example`, three NSX managers `chi1-nsx01` through `chi1-nsx03.corp.example` behind `chi1-nsx.corp.example`, three VCF Operations nodes `chi1-ops01` through `chi1-ops03.corp.example` behind `chi1-ops.corp.example`, and License Server `chi1-lic01.corp.example`. Use symbolic secret references, never literal credentials.

Before implementing, genuinely research the supported combinations and upgrade paths using the harness's own network access and currently reachable Broadcom-published compatibility, interoperability, upgrade-path, documentation, or knowledge sources. Also inspect the upstream `vmware/vcf-api-specs` installer specification at tag `9.1.0.0`. Do not treat the bundled snapshot as a substitute for live research. At the project root, record what you actually consulted in `research-consulted.md`. Use one Markdown bullet per source, and include the page title, reachable URL, access date, and the compatibility or upgrade-path fact obtained in every bullet. You may choose the sources and searches. If live material has changed since the fixture was pinned, note the difference there, but implement the pinned snapshot because it is the reproducible grading authority.

`generate` must create exactly these architecture artifacts inside the supplied output directory: `sddc-spec.json`, a pure `SddcSpec`; `topology-decision.json`, the capacity and site decision; and `migration-plan.json`, an ordered plan covering every inventory component once. The SDDC spec must validate as `#/components/schemas/SddcSpec` in `specifications/vcf-installer/vcf-installer-openapi.json`. The migration plan must validate against `fixtures/migration-plan.schema.json`. Use the component targets, actions, required gates, and precedence edges in `fixtures/compatibility-snapshot.json`; each step must name the inventory component, current version, target, action, and all of its gates. `topology-decision.json` must use schemaVersion `1.0`, selectedTopology `SINGLE_SITE_PRIMARY`, primarySite `CHI1`, recoverySite `OMA1`, recoveryPattern `ASYNC_BACKUP_RESTORE`, selectedHostCount 6, licensedCoresUsed 192, survivingCapacity values 160 cores / 2560 GiB / 25 TiB usable, RPO 15, and RTO 4. It must reject `STRETCHED_MANAGEMENT` with reasonCode `ENTITLEMENT_CORE_LIMIT` and requiredLicensedCores 256. Run `bash tests/run.sh` to verify the implementation.
